about.title: Malibu Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Malibu draws heavy foot traffic to its beaches, restaurants, and coastal shops, and that means property owners along corridors like Pacific Coast Highway and Malibu Canyon Road carry a real responsibility to keep walkways, stairs, and parking areas safe. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poorly lit stairwell causes a fall, the resulting injuries can be serious, and figuring out who is responsible isn't always simple. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why documenting the scene, getting names of witnesses, and preserving any surveillance footage matters right away, especially at commercial locations that often erase video after a short window. Our team doesn't practice law or promise any result. We simply evaluate premises liability claims in Malibu, help identify the notice issue and next steps, free of charge and with no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Us for Your Malibu Slip & Fall Claim

items.title: Understanding of the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises liability claims turn on whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help identify evidence showing that notice existed before your fall.

items.title: Urgency Around Preserving Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance footage at Malibu businesses and hazard conditions can disappear or get cleaned up within days. Acting quickly to request video and document the scene can matter a great deal to a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Awareness
items.desc: California is a pure comparative fault state, meaning you may still recover damages even if you were partly at fault, though the amount can be reduced. We can help address how fault-sharing arguments might affect your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Malibu?
items.answer: In California, the general deadline is two years from the date of the fall. If a government or public entity owns or maintains the property, such as a public beach access path or municipal lot, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's best to have this reviewed promptly so no window is missed.

items.question: What if the fall happened on a public beach or coastal access path near PCH?
items.answer: Beach areas and access paths near Pacific Coast Highway can involve a mix of private, state, and local ownership, which affects who is responsible and what deadlines apply. Identifying the correct property owner or public entity is an important early step. We can help sort out jurisdiction issues specific to Malibu's coastline.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, California law generally requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and had a chance to fix or warn about it. This is often established through maintenance logs, prior complaints, or how long the hazard existed. Photos, witness statements, and surveillance video can all help build this picture.
